claims.claim: The tutorial provides minimal direction, leaving beginners confused about core mechanics and progression.

citations.review_text:
Realm of the Mad God Exalt is surprisingly harsh on new players. The tutorial barely provides meaningful direction and while discovering things on your own can be fun, there’s a difference between mystery and confusion. When a new player asked when he should move to the next area, it became obvious the game never actually sets the stage for beginners. Core concepts like potion maxing aren’t explained at all, leaving players to stumble around until they figure it out—or give up.

The pet system, unfortunately, feels more like a curse than a blessing. First you need to randomly get an egg, then hope it rolls Heal and Magic Heal—the only abilities that really matter aside from Electric. Then you discover the real trap: everything about pets is tied to fame. You need fame to feed the pet, fame to upgrade the yard so you can feed it, and fame to fuse pets. And here’s the kicker: if you don’t feed or fuse correctly, you permanently ruin the pet and end up with something useless. Pets are such a massive part of the game that there’s even a status effect dedicated to disabling them, yet the entire system is locked behind either extreme grind or a paywall. Learning this was honestly demoralizing.

The leveling system for pets doesn’t help either. There are five rarities—Common, Uncommon, Rare, Legendary, Divine—each with its own max level, with Divine topping out at 100. To progress, you must fuse pets of the same rarity, and each fusion gives one of three results: Bad, Good or Max. Anything less than Max means your pet will never reach its full potential. So, you’re forced to keep feeding it gear or food until the game finally lets you fuse at the “correct” moment. One mistake and your pet is permanently inferior.

At this point, the game should either give new players a half‑maxed Common pet with Heal and Magic Heal, or rebalance things so players rely on teamwork instead of a Divine pet carrying them. As it stands, the system punishes beginners, rewards only the mos…

citations.review_text: can only play 1 character , you need money to unlock more slots .

*Playing on the standalone launcher* 

Came back to this after a few years break and I am pleasantly surprised at the changes they've made. Potions seem to drop much more often now from all sources and that makes the grind a LOT more bearable than it ever was before. The map biome change is a much welcome addition that makes it a lot less stale feeling after the nth time you're going to be leveling/statting a character. I'm not sure how to feel about the dungeon challenge changes just yet but so far it all seems positive and DECA is trying to breathe life back into the game. 

I do still see a lot of complaints about the new player experience and still being a relative newbie myself I can definitely see how its still plenty overwhelming for someone fresh but because of the pace of the game you can't really ease someone into it. It's a brutal bullet hell and the perma-death makes it doubly so and you'll find out right away what your patience level is. DECA claims to be working on the new player experience but the wiki and youtube are still your best friends for now and people in game seem to be willing to guide you in the right direction when you need it. Fortunately the gist is quite easy to grasp and there is no substitute for experience when it comes to surviving in this game.

I do love the item rarity and item modifier changes and it makes the high from seeing an ultra rare item drop even more satisfying. If you're a loot goblin like me this is definitely one of those games that loves to pour the loot on till you don't know what to do with it but beware that being completely f2p will limit your item vault and can make it feel quite bad at some points. They do give out extra vault space rewards every now and then but earning them usually comes at the cost of getting to late game and farming it which can be tedious and quite hard. 

Speaking on the monetization I don't have a problem with most of it. Yes, spending loads of money on the game will trivialize or bypa…

claims.claim: Reviewers report random disconnections that result in temporary lockouts from the game.

citations.review_text:
Great game, but im getting randomly disconnected and ip banned for 24 hrs. 
If i change to a different internet it lets me play again. No reply/help from customer support so far.

You will get randomly disconnected and then locked out of the game for anywhere from 1 to 30 minutes at a time. Judging by community feedback, this is a known issue that the developers have ignored for years.

When you finally do get to play, the end-game is a lagging mess. During 80-player boss events, the servers can't handle the load. Instead of balancing the game properly, the developers rely on artificially extending fights by making bosses completely immune to damage 90% of the time just so they don't get one-shot by the crowd. It’s a frustrating, lazy band-aid fix for poor game design. Cannot recommend.

claims.claim: Progression systems and mechanics like potions and pets are opaque, requiring players to rely heavily on external wikis, community guides, or YouTube videos to understand how to advance.

citations.review_text:
Despite the hours on record, all of mine are through Exalt Launcher. IGN NINJAUNICORN if you want to see stats and reference as a player with the hours put in and has done all the content, including all harder variations.

This game is for a very specific player. If you like high-focus gameplay, are willing to restart over and over, and enjoy perfecting your skills at content, this is the game for you. It is challenging, and has its flaws. But if you like a game where skill diff is very obvious, this game gives you that. Game has fun items to both experiment/have fun with and do crazy damage.

Discord and the Realm related servers are helpful, especially when trying to learn. But in this day and age you can go into the realm on any of the servers to find specific dungeons, join parties to find people, or go to USEast2 and just join dungeons popped in the nexus. My #1 advice if you're ever struggling is to read the Realmeye Wiki or YouTube videos and learn how the mechanics actually work. You can usually reverse engineer a solution from there (or learn a safespot).

Cheats are rampant in this game. Don't like them personally, unfortunately DECA doesn't deal with it well. However, unless they are giga-blasting everything and ruining the challenge of content, they have little affect on you. I strongly recommend not using them, as every person I know who used cheats quits relatively quickly afterwards, because the fun of the game comes from achieving glory after all the failure. If you play and get tempted, I promise it completely ruins the fun of this game for no one but yourself. 

If you play, have fun exploring, play with confidence as its way more fun to play aggressive, die, and learn than to leech. Push your gameplay and the difficulty of dungeons and this game will be worthwhile for you. If you choose to really get invested, be prepared to die, accept it as a grueling learning process, and that it gets easier to rebuild as you learn more.

Everything is on external wikipedia. Thats a bonus and a minus at once, depending entirely on how much do you want to invest in this bullet hell.

The game features all sorts of content and aesthetics. Once again, kitchen sink of features, which is a bonus and a minus depending on how much you value your artistic direction.

Graphics hold up, but they aren't exactly made to ever go out of style.
It's an aight vertical RPG with a decently diverse endgame, with some multiplayer elements, if you count randoms dying mid boss as multiplayer, or the occasional PPE paladin providing negative DPS.

Speaking as someone who played everything and stuck with the class assassin, I think the progression in this game is very opaque and you never really know which dungeons should you do for which class, because the game is so old, most of this knowledge is limited to old veterans busy doing their daily routines, or to piecing it together from a dozen wiki articles + writing down your own flowcharts of farming for items.

Honestly, if you're here for a simple experience, just pick any of the long range classess like wizard, priest, necromancer, sorcerer, summoner and go ham on the nearest dungeon, repeat untill full UT 8/8 or death.

I just keep trying to come back to this game and I just never can anymore. I used to play this back when it was on a website of all things, I think this was like 8+ years back. I played religiously then, and in the past 4 years I have switched to Steam and then ultimately stopped.

The evolution of the game has been neat, but the cash grab has really been what has developed. The game  has gone from a challenge to... almost an idle game, just waiting for someone who DOES spend money to waste a bunch so you can get keys and such. The mechanics of pets and potions are so integral to the game, but never touched on meaningfully and leaving those new or just unfamiliar to the mechanics at a complete loss for how to really use them to progress.

Overall, I can't say I would recommend the game anymore. The P2W aspect is nearly Pay2Play for it's realistic limitations, and while the core of the gameplay and mechanics are till there, everything now involved with "playing" the game has changed to feel as a corporate and hollow cash grab for the last few years :c

claims.claim: The title relies heavily on monetization, pay-to-win elements, and tight storage management.

citations.review_text: Has an interesting and satisyfing game loop, but overall it's too pay to win for me to enjoy it.

Restarting after playing the game on Kongregate back in the Adobe Flash version as a kid was fairly interesting. Uncovering what I missed years ago and being at level 20 with the world still dangerous leaves the game fresh, at least for a while. The new music is interesting with new composers on the team, and the environment is definitely more vibrant with various revamps to dungeons and a bunch of care put into them. However, as I kept going I started having many gripes with the game. Tight storage management, heavy monetization, occasional dips in quality, and a harsh learning curve makes me reluctant to recommend this game to many people.

In the beginning I was puzzled on the weird distribution of server population. Various servers nexuses’ weren’t full, save for EUWest or USEast, there’s a lot of bots in the nexus that advertise websites, inundations for mystery boxes, and bubbles on items that disappear soon; the numerous things you can do with realm gold is still the same, if not more: buying storage, mystery boxes, and a single name change for 1,000 realm gold... so pick your name wisely. Then you enter a realm, some cave-like sprite, by going up and start exploring.

Exploring the world and dungeons is the whole game, and is often entertaining and invigorating as you dodge bullet patterns and kill numerous enemies. Obtaining special equipment and items in “white bags” called Set Tier and Untiered items (or called ST/UT; both are unique and have gimmicks in functionality for equipment) is necessary outside of paying, and surviving becomes more difficult as you enter harder dungeons found in later parts of the world. Furthermore, these are necessary to get your character stronger through stat potions that are permanently applied to a character like increasing damage dealt or fire rate or the maximum damage you can take before you die. This element of skill in dodging bullets hooks a lot of people and despite my lack of experience at shoot ‘em ups (or called s…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a steep learning curve with a terrible tutorial and onboarding experience for new players.

citations.review_text: its an incredibly fun and challenging game. its confusing to learn at first, the tutorial and new player onboarding are terrible. but once you learn the intricacies of the game, its one that will eat up hours of your time. it is my all time favorite game, despite its issues. i used to play it 10 years ago when it was still a flash game and i was still a teenager. fair warning though, this is a rogue like mmorpg. if you are going to play this game, dont be afraid to die when you are first starting out. look at it like an extended tutorial at first. learn the map, learn some dungeons, and get comfortable with the game. there is a decently steep learning curve, and dying means losing all of your items you were carrying. the risk of death is what makes this game truly great once you get the hang of it. the late game dungeons are high risk high reward, claiming the characters of even veteran players.

This is a very awkward game for me to review, personally i think the game itself is great, however, there are a lot of issues with it from the perspective of a new player... I'm going to do a basic pro and con list

Pros
-great character customization
-everything is free to play
-unlimited content
-loot and shoot bullethell

Cons
-unstable servers
-toxic community 
-over ran by bots/clients
-very steep difficulty curve for new players
-heavily incentivized to spend money to progress

with that being said, i do think rotmg is a really fun game to play, i realistically have over 5k hours (low estimate) since mid 2010's when i started playing on flash, but, with the negative aspects of the game, i cant recommend anyone play this and would suggest alternative mmo rpgs
genuinely generational game concept, getting into it is hard tho

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's core gameplay loop as creating a character, leveling, gaining gear, raiding, and losing carried items upon death.

its an incredibly fun and challenging game. its confusing to learn at first, the tutorial and new player onboarding are terrible. but once you learn the intricacies of the game, its one that will eat up hours of your time. it is my all time favorite game, despite its issues. i used to play it 10 years ago when it was still a flash game and i was still a teenager. fair warning though, this is a rogue like mmorpg. if you are going to play this game, dont be afraid to die when you are first starting out. look at it like an extended tutorial at first. learn the map, learn some dungeons, and get comfortable with the game. there is a decently steep learning curve, and dying means losing all of your items you were carrying. the risk of death is what makes this game truly great once you get the hang of it. the late game dungeons are high risk high reward, claiming the characters of even veteran players.

I stopped playing this game about 10 years ago because it was slowly going downhill. Only to find myself crawling back because I mentioned rotmg in a comment section. Someone told me that it was back and better than ever. So, I had to redownload it and give it a try. The core loops still the same but now, it seems easier than ever to hit "early end game" which use to feel like it would take ages. This game has impressed me once again. For being a simple a browser game to having full support almost 15 years later is insane. 

The core loops simple. 
Make character. 
Level character. 
Gear character. 
Raid. 
Die to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or greed. 
Repeat

Its such an addicting game and for no good reason either.
I will always recommend this game but take my word.

Realm of the Mad Infi-load.
What can I say? For nostalgia's sake the game is fun. I first played ROTMG back when it was a browser game. Honestly, Deca does more with the game than people give them credit for. They've developed new content and new classes and pushed the game beyond its nostalgia borders. I, for one, think all of that is excellent. But you will hear players complain about "the servers." 

Okay, this is incorrect. The game does not crash, disconnect you, and infinite load you (infi-load) because of the servers, but because of the bad coding of the game. 

And if you want to talk about an ULTRA TOXIC COMMUNITY in MMOs this might be the one. The amount of political toxicity you will see in game is unreal, uncalled for, unmoderated, and unfun. Toxic interactions are common as well as toxic usernames. I am a true free speech believer, and with that comes toxicity, but in the end no effort is made to address these issues or the prevailing issue of cheaters. 

Cheaters affect the game balance by trivializing content, intentionally grief killing other players, and then acting like they are good. I cannot wrap my mind around cheaters who are elitist, but here we are. They intentionally crash people and crash servers. But if there is a reason I can't recommend the game, it has to be the disconnects and crashes. My guild leader quit the game for OSRS because he would buy keys and get disconnected on purchased keys. He would also die on a character carrying ten keys which is hilariously noob like lol. But anyway. 

The game has gone the narcissistic path of all live-service games; a path of "you have to keep your eyes on the game," "you have to log in", "you have to grind." It quickly turns from fun and challenging nostalgia into a chore. 
I don't recommend Realm of the Mad God. Your time can be better spent elsewhere.

So, RotMG is a great game overall, challenging, rewarding, and sometimes rage inducing.

The problem is that Deca doesn't know what the term "Competent servers" means. Their entire network goes down at least once a day and it is barely uncommon to be booted out for no fault of your own doing something as simple as going back to the nexus or, god forbid, having to Alt+F4 because the game decided to lag out and make everything drift as if they were on the world's slipperiest ice.

And mind you. they reset the servers daily too. They give warning for this, but they crash so often they might as well not even reset em.

And mind you, this review was caused by this exact case happening. I had to Alt+F4 cause the servers took a ♥♥♥♥, and they legit crashed for awhile.

For fun, I'm gonna list all server crashes I've had since writing this review: 7
